title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial-generation protocol (one candidate per intent shared by both arms). The guarded arm validated the shared candidate with a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and applied ≤1 deterministic repair iteration when the validator reported repairable faults. Execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator under adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Primary hypothesis tested with the exact McNemar two-sided (binomial) formulation yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We summarize validator checks, the deterministic repair heuristics and invocation rule, the exact statistical implementation used for small discordant counts, and operational limitations (shared-generation estimand, synthetic tasks, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity). All prompts, responses, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction: Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) tasks with generative large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises reliability and safety concerns: LLMs can produce syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe or incomplete configurations (incorrect ordering, omitted prerequisites, or protected-interface violations). Prior work proposes verifier-augmented and repair architectures to reduce such failures, but rigorous, execution-grounded evidence evaluating their marginal efficacy is limited. We preregistered a narrowly scoped paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard raises the proportion of emulator-executable configurations relative to accepting ungated LLM outputs. To isolate the deterministic validator/repair operator’s capacity to correct the same LLM candidate, we used a shared-initial-generation protocol: a single candidate per intent was produced and fed to both the ungated baseline and the guarded validator/repair flow. Our principal contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) reporting exact paired counts, the inferential treatment appropriate for small discordant counts, a concise description of the deterministic repair operator, and an artifact-grounded discussion of operational implications and limitations.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and prototype studies document LLM applications to intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilot assistance while reporting hallucinations and schema violations as recurring failure modes. Mitigation strategies reported in adjacent domains include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding, live schema grounding, and verifier-assisted repair loops; these reduce but do not eliminate structured-output errors. Formal-method verifiers (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) can detect reachability/isolation violations but face fidelity and scalability trade-offs when representing control-plane dynamics. Our study complements these works by measuring the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair stage applied to an identical shared candidate — an estimand that isolates deterministic repair-on-same-candidate efficacy rather than the wider question of guard architectures that permit independent re-sampling or multiple LLM attempts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The experiment was preregistered and frozen before execution (preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd...ff68). Confirmatory sample: n=200 natural-language change intents curated to span single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Paired design and estimand: shared-initial-generation (one LLM candidate per intent shared by both arms); primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Model and budget: declared model gpt-5-mini; maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized hosted-model calls used = 201. Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator identified as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator behavior and version recorded in scoring artifacts). Outcome definition: an episode is successful when the validator reports validation_after.valid == true after applying the candidate to the emulator. Missingness and retries: transient provider/API errors received a single automatic retry per preregistered policy; provider/API failures are counted as failures in the primary analysis. Deterministic validator behavior: the archived validator traces show three stages: (1) syntactic parse and normalization of CLI-like lines into canonical tokens and a normalized_configuration string (parse failures are treated as invalid), (2) structural and workflow checks enforcing required-command presence, dependency/make-before-break patterns, group/activity constraints and protected-interface checks, and (3) final-state simulation that applies the normalized configuration to the emulator model and compares observed final_state fields to the task’s expected_final_state. Violation-code families used in artifacts include SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR, MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, and TRANSIENT_RULE_VIOLATION. Deterministic repair operator (concise algorithmic description): the guarded pipeline invoked a deterministic repair operator when the validator returned violation_count>0 and the violations matched repairable classes (primarily MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND or DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION). The operator performs deterministic, rule-based transformations to the normalized_configuration without calling the LLM: (a) insert specific missing commands identified by the validator (e.g., required shutdown/restore lines), (b) reorder command blocks to satisfy dependency/make-before-break constraints, and (c) preserve protected-interface statements and unspecified state per task constraints. Repair invocation rule: repair is invoked at most once per episode (bounded repair budget ≤1) and only when the validator labels are within the operator’s repairable family. All per-episode validator inputs/outputs and repair traces are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results: Execution accounting and raw outcomes: all planned episodes completed (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures; hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=199, n10=1 (guarded-only), n01=0 (baseline-only), n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Deterministic repair and failure accounting: initial validator failures (validation_before.valid == false) occurred in exactly 1 episode; syntactic parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1 (the single repair converted the validator-failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration and produced the sole guarded-only success). Missingness: no missing or unscorable episodes were recorded in confirmatory analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Statistical inference, exact implementation: the preregistered primary hypothesis test used the exact McNemar two-sided test implemented via the binomial test on discordant counts: under the null the count of discordant pairs in one direction follows Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5). With observed n10 = 1 and n01 = 0, the two-sided exact p-value equals 1.0 (artifact: analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples and seed 1729, yielding [0.0, 0.015] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Interpretation vs. preregistered power: the preregistered design targeted a detectable absolute effect of 0.15 assuming a baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline (0.995) diverged from that assumption and materially reduces ability to detect large absolute improvements. The bootstrap CI excludes effects ≥0.015 and therefore excludes the preregistered 0.15 effect in this confirmatory outcome distribution. Secondary planned analyses (repair-iteration yield curve, failure-taxonomy counts) were constrained by the small number of repair events and are reported descriptively in the archived analysis artifacts rather than inferentially.
sections.discussion: Estimand and operational framing: the shared-initial-generation estimand isolates whether a deterministic repair operator can correct the same LLM candidate judged invalid by a deterministic validator. It does not evaluate guarded architectures that permit independent re-sampling, multi-iteration LLM repairs, or broader active remediation policies; those operational designs can realize larger gains at higher model-call cost but were outside this study’s preregistered budget. Practical implications drawn from artifact-backed findings: (1) on a curated confirmatory distribution where gpt-5-mini produced near-perfect candidates, bounded deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yields marginal improvement (1 additional pass out of 200); (2) deterministic validators remain valuable as assurance gates and for generating diagnostic violation codes that enable automated repair heuristics or human escalation; (3) in harder or adversarial distributions, or under an independent-resampling estimand, verifier-assisted architectures that allow additional LLM calls or larger repair budgets are expected to yield larger practical benefits. Threats to validity: internal validity concerns include prompt sensitivity limited by a single model and prompt template, the shared-generation choice that isolates repair but reduces evaluation of independent-resampling designs, and the bounded repair budget. Construct validity concerns include emulator and validator fidelity: the Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior deterministically but do not capture all production dynamics (for example, asynchronous BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies). External validity concerns include single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic curated task set that may not encompass real-world NetOps heterogeneity or adversarial intents. Reproducibility and artifact availability: all prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis CSVs and logs, and the full execution manifest are archived in the public evidence bundle referenced by the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). The preregistration SHA is provided above; analysis artifacts record bootstrap parameters (seed 1729, 10,000 resamples) and the exact McNemar implementation used. Reviewer-requested items and constraints: per-episode validator rule families and repair invocation criteria are summarized above and documented in scoring/validator traces. Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy/medium/hard/very_hard) for the confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and are available in the artifact bundle; the preregistered confirmatory run completed across the curated difficulty mix recorded there. Operational recommendation: practitioners should adopt deterministic validator gates to detect and document structured faults, and consider resource-weighted policies (bounded re-sampling, iterative repair budgets, or human escalation thresholds) tuned to expected baseline LLM quality and operational risk tolerances.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a bounded generate–verify–repair guard for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The artifact-backed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]), which excludes the preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect due to a realized near-ceiling baseline. For the confirmatory distribution and estimand studied, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a negligible marginal improvement; broader operational value depends on task difficulty, estimand choice (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling), model capability, repair budget, and emulator fidelity. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multivendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and enhanced emulator fidelity (control-plane timing) to better characterize when GVR guards provide substantive operational benefits.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (provider recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; manifest hash recorded in the execution manifest) and may be inspected in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty counts; that per-task metadata underlies task curation but was not summarized as numeric counts in this manuscript.
